NORM_GEOMETRY.implementation_path_notes: Closed-form Lp norm: element-wise difference, absolute value, power, summation, root extraction. All float64 arithmetic. No external LP solver required. Degenerate paths: p=1 (no root), p=2 (standard square root), p=inf (max of absolute values). Fully deterministic without any external library or pivot-rule policy. Blocked scopes: lp_norm_computation, distance_emission.

TRANSPORT.implementation_path_notes: Discrete balanced optimal transport on a finite cost matrix. Degenerate cases (m=1, n=1, 1x1) are closed-form float64 weighted sums requiring no LP. General m*n case requires an LP solver; solver variant, pivot rule, and tie-breaking strategy are not yet locked. Balance tolerance (epsilon_rel) not yet locked. LP solver non-determinism risk for degenerate problems (multiple optimal transport plans) requires explicit tie-breaking policy before implementation can begin.

recommendation_rationale.blocking_factors_for_transport: LP solver variant not declared; pivot rule not declared; tie-breaking strategy not declared; balance tolerance epsilon_rel not locked; cost matrix magnitude bound not locked. All five must be resolved before TRANSPORT implementation begins.
recommendation_rationale.norm_geometry_relative_advantage: No solver dependency risk (NONE vs HIGH for TRANSPORT). Lower deterministic implementation risk (LOW vs MEDIUM). Smaller expected test surface (SMALL vs MEDIUM). Fixture uniqueness guaranteed for all valid test cases.
recommendation_rationale.primary_reason: NORM_GEOMETRY is recommended as the first implementation path because it is closed-form and has no LP solver dependency. All Lp norm computation paths are deterministic float64 arithmetic with no external library or pivot-rule policy decisions required. Five locked constants are needed before NORM_GEOMETRY implementation can begin; all are well-defined and operator-decidable without external policy discovery.
recommendation_rationale.secondary_reason: TRANSPORT implementation requires seven locked constants, five of which depend on LP solver policy decisions (solver variant, pivot rule, tie-breaking rule, balance tolerance, max problem size). These cannot be resolved without explicit operator policy choices that are independent of NORM_GEOMETRY implementation.

required_decisions.description: Confirm that all element-wise differences, power operations, summation accumulation, and root extraction must use float64. Float32 excluded.
Declare the exact sentinel value used to represent p=inf in input data. Required before implementation to ensure deterministic branch selection.
Declare the maximum allowed element magnitude in input vectors. Required to bound power overflow risk.
Declare the maximum allowed p value. Required to bound power overflow risk for finite p.
Confirm the complete enumeration of NOT_COMPUTABLE conditions: empty vector, p < 1.0, mismatched lengths, non-finite element, power overflow.
Declare the exact LP solver variant to be used for general m*n balanced transport problems. Must be a deterministic solver with a fixed algorithm family.
Declare the exact pivot rule for the LP solver. Stochastic or randomized pivot rules excluded.
Declare the tie-breaking rule for degenerate transport problems with multiple optimal transport plans. Required for deterministic fixture matching.
Declare the exact relative balance tolerance epsilon_rel. Planned value: 1e-9 * max(sum(supply), sum(demand)). Must be locked before implementation.
Declare the maximum allowed m*n problem size (number of LP decision variables). Required to bound LP solve time and memory usage.
Declare the maximum allowed cost matrix entry value. Required to bound float64 overflow risk in the LP objective accumulation.
Confirm the complete enumeration of NOT_COMPUTABLE conditions: empty supply/demand, unbalanced, negative element, non-finite value, cost_matrix shape mismatch.
